questions.text: For an RNN with h_t = f(h_(t-1), x_t), why do additional GPU cores alone not eliminate the sequential dependency across tokens?

options.A: The next hidden state requires the preceding hidden state to be computed.
options.B: Every token requires its own separately trained copy of the model.
options.C: The hidden-state vector must grow in width after every token.
options.D: The recurrence must first construct a dense attention matrix.

questions.explanation: The hidden-state recurrence imposes an ordered dependency chain even if individual operations within each step can run in parallel.

questions.text: A dense attention score matrix contains one entry per ordered token pair. If context length triples, how many times as many score entries are required?
questions.explanation: The matrix has N squared entries. Tripling length gives (3N) squared = 9N squared.

questions.text:
What does this recurrence return?

```python
h = 0.0
for x in [10.0, 0.0, 0.0]:
    h = 0.9 * h + x
print(h)
```
questions.explanation: The successive hidden states are 10.0, 9.0, and 8.1.
